text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (specifically Lutzia or Phlebotomus species) secondary to immunosuppression from Crohn's disease and prior uveitis treatment. The history of an insect bite, ulcerative lesion on the leg, and specific comorbidities strongly suggests this diagnosis over cellulitis or a simple bacterial infection. I will request a skin biopsy for histopathology and PCR to confirm the presence of Leishmania amastigotes.
